plan.title: Heart WT vs KO x Vehicle vs Drug interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is whether the drug acts differently in KO than in WT heart tissue — a genotype x treatment interaction question on a 2x2 factorial design (genotype: WT/KO; treatment: vehicle/drug; 4 replicates per cell, 16 samples total, 12000 genes, raw Salmon counts). All scripting is Python per the user's constraint, using PyDESeq2 (the Python re-implementation of the DESeq2 workflow, Muzellec et al. 2023, Bioinformatics, PMID 37669147) rather than R DESeq2. The plan follows the grounded procedure from the knowledge service: (1) sample-structure QC on variance-stabilized, design-blind counts to check that samples cluster by genotype/treatment and to catch outliers before any test runs; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest cell size) so the test retains power and independent filtering downstream does the rest; (3) fit PyDESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle), and test the interaction coefficient (genotype[KO].treatment[drug]) with the Wald test — this coefficient IS the answer to 'does the drug act differently in KO vs WT'; (4) report the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT; drug vs vehicle within KO) alongside the interaction contrast, because the interaction alone does not say whether the drug does anything in either genotype; (5) shrink log2 fold changes (apeglm for the single coefficients, ashr for the summed simple-effect contrasts) and rank on the shrunken value in tables while ranking the GSEA input on the unshrunken Wald statistic; (6) BH-adjust p-values within each of the three contrasts separately, inspecting the p-value histogram first; (7) run preranked GSEA (gseapy, since fgsea is R-only and everything must be Python) against the human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets staged in the reference store, once per contrast; (8) an integrated report with QC/fit diagnostics, the three contrast tables (with both raw and shrunken LFC), enrichment tables with leading-edge genes, and a full reproducibility record. Given a 4-replicates-per-cell design, DESeq2's automatic count-outlier handling sets some gene p-values to NA per cell rather than replacing counts (that behavior applies at >=7 replicates) — this is flagged for the report. The interaction coefficient is a difference-of-differences with inherently larger standard error than either main effect, so power to detect it is intrinsically lower than for the simple effects at n=4/cell; this is stated as a limitation, not silently absorbed.
